title: Olivia and the Sticky Floor
subtitle: Rough things hold on
author: Olivia's Shelf
blurb: Olivia slides on a smooth bench, then stops on a rough mat, and learns that friction is a quiet grab between things that touch.

magic.launch: The little rocket pushed the air, and the air pushed back.
magic.drop: Everything falls. That pull has a name: gravity.

openai.instructions: Warm, clear storyteller reading a science picture book to a child. Curious, never lecturing. Pause at full stops.

pages.heading: A sudden stop
pages.text: {Olivia} slid on the smooth {workshop} bench — then her shoe caught on a rough mat. "{Elon:elon/look}," she said. "The floor grabbed me."

pages.heading: A quiet grab
pages.text: "That grab is {friction}," said {Elon:elon/teach}. "When two things touch, they hold on a little."

pages.heading: Rough holds more
pages.text: Olivia rubbed a smooth lid, then a rough {stone}. "Rough things grab {more}," said Elon. "Smooth things let go."

pages.heading: Why we can walk
pages.text: "Friction helps you {walk}," said {Elon:elon/teach}. "Without it, your shoes would skate. A rocket needs a push. Walking needs a grab."

pages.heading: Useful and sticky
pages.text: A rolling cart slowed on the floor. "Friction also {steals} speed," said Elon. "Sometimes that keeps us safe."

pages.heading: Keep asking why
pages.text: "Why do rubbing hands feel warm?" asked {Olivia:olivia/ask}. "Friction makes the tiny bits {dance}," said {Elon:elon/teach}. "Ask why again tomorrow."

end.heading: The End
end.text: Friction is a quiet grab. Rough holds more. It helps you walk — and warms your hands.
end.prompt: What would you slide, then stop, tomorrow?

credits: Painted for Olivia's Shelf. Elon is a picture-book inventor who teaches physics; this is not a biography.
